湾区长者坐车省钱指南: Senior transit discounts in the Bay Area
65 岁办 Senior Clipper 卡；旧金山低收入居民 65 岁起可免费: At 65, get a Senior Clipper card; lower-income San Francisco residents 65+ can ride Muni free; paratransit for those who can’t ride regular transit
年满 65 岁可以办长者 Clipper 卡：BART 票价减 62.5%，Mu: At 65 you can get a Senior Clipper card: 62.5% off BART, $1.40 senior single rides on Muni, $1 on VTA and SamTrans, $1.37 a senior local ride with Clipper on AC Transit. San Francisco residents 65+ with family income at or below 100% of Bay Area median can apply to ride Muni free. Anyone who can't use regular transit because of a disability or health condition can apply for ADA paratransit.

在湾区坐车，65 岁是省钱的分界线：满 65 岁就能办长者 Clipper 卡，: For Bay Area transit, 65 is where the savings start: from 65 you can get a Senior Clipper card and pay senior fares on BART, Muni, VTA, SamTrans and AC Transit. Get the card first, then see whether your city has an extra free program; for anyone who can't ride regular transit, there is pre-booked door-to-door paratransit.

BART's fiscal year 2026–27 budget, adopted in June 2026 and running through June 30, 2027, has no fare increase and keeps the senior discount; a separate contingency plan for a funding shortfall awaits further BART Board decisions and is not a set of decided fares.
Muni（旧金山）：用 Clipper 单程 $1.40，120 分钟内有效；现: Muni (San Francisco): single ride $1.40 with Clipper, good for 120 minutes; $1.50 cash; monthly pass $43; cable car $4 before 7 a.m. or after 9 p.m. (2026 fares; MuniMobile stopped selling single rides on September 1, 2026). From January 4, 2027: $1.50 single ride on Clipper (cash stays $1.50), $45 monthly pass, and $6 for the cable car before 7 a.m. or after 9 p.m.
VTA（南湾）：单程 $1；日票 $3 和月票 $30 只能用 Clipper，: VTA (South Bay): single ride $1; the $3 day pass and $30 monthly pass are Clipper only, not sold for cash. A single ride paid with Clipper includes 2 hours of free transfers, and Clipper stops charging for the day once you have paid the $3 day-pass price. These are the current fares on VTA's site as of October 17, 2026; the site has no announcement of 2027 fare changes.
SamTrans（半岛）：单程 Clipper $1.00、现金 $1.10，日: SamTrans (Peninsula): single ride $1.00 on Clipper, $1.10 cash; day pass $2.00; monthly pass $27.00.
AC Transit（东湾）：长者本地单程用 Clipper $1.37、现金: AC Transit (East Bay): a senior local single ride is $1.37 on Clipper or $1.50 in cash, about half the adult fare; paying with Clipper, local rides cost at most $3 a day and $41.50 a month (fares from July 1, 2026; as of October 17, 2026 the site had no announcement of 2027 fare changes).
旧金山：65 岁及以上低收入居民免费坐 Muni: San Francisco: free Muni for lower-income residents 65+
SFMTA 的“长者免费坐 Muni”（Free Muni for Senior: SFMTA's Free Muni for Seniors gives San Francisco residents 65+ with gross family income at or below 100% of Bay Area median free Muni rides, cable cars included, on a Clipper card. Applying online is fastest: enter your registered Senior Clipper card's serial number, or upload proof of age if you don't have one. You can also download the application in Chinese and mail or drop it off at the SFMTA Customer Service Center (11 South Van Ness Avenue, ATTN: FREE MUNI). Approval takes up to 3 weeks with an existing Clipper card and up to 4 weeks if a new card is needed.
三种优惠看的条件不一样：长者 Clipper 卡只看年龄（65 岁及以上），不看: The three discounts have different rules: the Senior Clipper card depends only on age (65 or older), not income; Free Muni requires living in San Francisco with family income at or below 100% of the Bay Area median; Clipper START is for people 19–64 with income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Qualifying for one does not enroll you in another; apply for each separately.
SFMTA 写明：这个项目在继续，卡上原来显示的 2025 年 6 月 30 日: SFMTA says the program continues: the June 30, 2025 expiration date some cards showed was updated to 2028 on July 1, 2025.
未满 65 岁、有残障：Clipper Access 卡（原名 RTC）: Under 65 with a disability: Clipper Access (formerly RTC)
Clipper Access 是给未满 65 岁、有符合条件残障的乘客办的优惠卡: Clipper Access is the discount card for riders under 65 with qualifying disabilities, also 62.5% off BART. There are two paths: Basic eligibility (for example a Medicare card held by someone under 65, a DMV placard registration receipt, or existing ADA paratransit eligibility) and Medical eligibility (certified by a California licensed professional). When you apply, transit agency staff photocopy your documents and take your photo. Elders 65 and over simply get a Senior card.
出门困难：申请 ADA 辅助交通（paratransit）: Hard to get out: apply for ADA paratransit
因为残障或健康原因没法自己坐公交、地铁的人，可以申请 ADA 辅助交通：预约厢型: People who can't use buses or trains on their own because of a disability or health condition can apply for ADA paratransit: pre-booked van or taxi rides. In San Francisco it's SF Paratransit: general questions 415.351.7000 (Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4:45 p.m.), SF Access reservations 415.285.6945, option 2 (daily 7 a.m.–6 p.m.). In the East Bay it's East Bay Paratransit, run by AC Transit and BART: (510) 287-5000, during AC Transit and BART operating hours, within ¾ mile of a bus route or BART station, with a rider guide in Chinese on its site. In Santa Clara County it's VTA ACCESS: call (408) 321-2381 to apply for eligibility (the application form comes in Chinese), and once approved, book rides 1–3 days ahead at (408) 321-2380 (8 a.m. until before 5 p.m.). In other counties, ask the local transit agency's paratransit office.
Clipper START 坐湾区公共交通单程五折，三个条件一起看：住在湾区、1: Clipper START takes 50% off single rides on Bay Area transit. The three conditions go together: you live in the Bay Area, you are 19–64, and your household income before taxes is at or under the limit (CalFresh participants qualify automatically). The 2026 limit is $31,920 for a one-person household, set at 200% of the federal poverty level; the 2027 limit has not been published. Apply online and upload proof of identity and income; processing can take up to 30 days. San Francisco's Lifeline monthly pass moves to Clipper START on January 1, 2027.
